title: Keeping Cows
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/102d3b50e173130cf743989c3420bac69643467e.png)A cow. CC BY-SA 3.0 by Kim Hansen on Wikimedia Commons

Farmer Kiki has $42$ cows. Their field can be thought of as a grid where each cell is a square with a side length of one metre. According to strict regulations of the German Cow Perimeter Conglomerate, the cows must graze on a fenced area that is exactly $a$ square metres large.

Unfortunately, Farmer Kiki's supplier messed up their order of fence pieces. Instead of mostly straight fence pieces and just a few corner fence pieces, they only received an enormous amount of corner fence pieces. There are even more pieces than would fit on the field. One corner fence looks like this:

```
....
.O#.
.#..
....
```

Here '`O`' denotes the center of the fence, '`#`' denotes the sides of the fence, and '`.`' denotes empty space.

Farmer Kiki can rotate and move each corner fence grid-aligned. How may they place them such that there is a side-connected component of exactly $a$ empty cells that is surrounded by fence pieces? More exactly, for each interior cell of that component all four orthogonal neighbours have to either also be an interior empty cell or part of a fence piece.

Farmer Kiki's field is $100 \times 100$ cells large and they cannot place any fence piece outside this area.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fe30100777d60f3a9d1b464820cfd91cbc634710.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bd90c8072f5b7c575c669196e6b6a8b281ea5c72.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1d4520e272e85bc2cc294209d9b758fa4775de47.png)Two valid and one invalid construction for the first sample with fenced area $4$. The left construction represents the given sample answer. On the right, the four interior cells are not side-connected.

## Input

The input consists of:

- One line with an integer $a$ ($1\leq a \leq 5000$), the exact number of cells the cow enclosure should contain.

## Output

Output two integers $h$ and $w$ ($1 \leq h, w \leq 100$), the height and width of the used area. Then output the fence placement represented by $h$ strings of length $w$ containing only '`#`', '`.`', and '`O`' (the letter, not the digit '`0`').

If there are multiple valid solutions, you may output any one of them.
statementZhMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/102d3b50e173130cf743989c3420bac69643467e.png)一头奶牛。图片由 Kim Hansen 发布于 Wikimedia Commons，采用 CC BY-SA 3.0 许可协议

农场主 Kiki 有 $42$ 头奶牛。它们的牧场可以看作一个网格，每个格子都是边长为一米的正方形。根据德国奶牛围栏联合会的严格规定，奶牛必须在一块用围栏围住、面积恰好为 $a$ 平方米的区域内吃草。

不幸的是，农场主 Kiki 的供应商把围栏组件的订单弄错了。原本订购的组件应当大多是直线形围栏，只有少量拐角形围栏，但他们收到的却全是数量极其庞大的拐角形围栏，甚至多到整个牧场都放不下。一个拐角形围栏如下所示：

```
....
.O#.
.#..
....
```

其中，'`O`' 表示围栏的中心，'`#`' 表示围栏的两侧，'`.`' 表示空地。

农场主 Kiki 可以旋转和平移每个拐角形围栏，但必须使其与网格对齐。他们应当如何摆放这些围栏，才能围出一个恰好包含 $a$ 个空格子、通过公共边连通的连通块？更准确地说，对于该连通块内部的每个格子，它上下左右的四个相邻格子都必须也是内部的空格子，或属于某个围栏组件。

农场主 Kiki 的牧场大小为 $100 \times 100$ 个格子，任何围栏组件都不能放到这个区域之外。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fe30100777d60f3a9d1b464820cfd91cbc634710.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bd90c8072f5b7c575c669196e6b6a8b281ea5c72.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1d4520e272e85bc2cc294209d9b758fa4775de47.png)对于第一个样例，图中给出了两种合法构造和一种不合法构造，围住的面积均为 $4$。左边的构造对应给出的样例答案。右边的四个内部格子无法通过公共边连通。

## 输入格式

输入包括：

- 一行，包含一个整数 $a$ ($1\leq a \leq 5000$)，表示奶牛围栏内应恰好包含的格子数。

## 输出格式

输出两个整数 $h$ 和 $w$ ($1 \leq h, w \leq 100$)，表示所用区域的高度和宽度。然后输出 $h$ 个长度为 $w$ 的字符串，表示围栏的摆放方式，字符串只能包含 '`#`'、'`.`' 和 '`O`'（字母，而非数字 '`0`'）。

如果存在多个合法方案，你可以输出其中任意一个。
